key_insight: A hybrid β-VAE-GAN plus sensor-conditioned Transformer can learn a compact, physically interpretable latent model of near-wall turbulence and forecast its intermittent dynamics far beyond the initial observation window.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical CFD surrogate for wall-bounded flows, enabling reduced-cost long-horizon prediction from sparse sensors while preserving key turbulent energy and regeneration-cycle behavior.
method: β-VAE-GAN compresses full flow fields into a low-dimensional latent space.
A sensor-conditioned Transformer predicts latent evolution over time.
Easy Attention and AdaLN-Zero reduce attention cost and condition forecasts on measurements.
evidence_signal: On the Minimal Flow Unit at Reτ=200, the model reconstructs 87% of turbulent kinetic energy in a 4D latent space and achieves 82% TKE reconstruction with forecasts sustained over 17,288 t+ from only 128 t+ of initialization data.
watch_item: Rare extreme-amplitude events are attenuated, suggesting the low-dimensional bottleneck may underrepresent intermittent outliers.
paper_title: A Hybrid Generative Reduced-Order Model for the Minimal Flow Unit
